neighbours.label: A physical feature or material described by what it does for flow: fires on the word leading into a transport function (improve water drainage, heat dissipation, air circulation); reversed output promotes ' conductivity', ' drainage', ' diffusion', ' channels'
fire: Coarse sand is worked into the flower bed because it improves water drainage around the roots.
Aluminium ribs along the motor housing are there to improve heat transfer to the air.
Slots in the brake disc promote air circulation and keep the pads cool.
The porous ceramic wick gives good water transport from the tank to the soil.
A thin graphite pad under the chip provides better heat conduction to the cover.
Raised ridges on the greenhouse floor improve water runoff after each watering.
The open weave of the cloth allows good air flow through the filter.
Crushed stone beneath the path helps water drainage during heavy storms.
quiet: Coarse sand was delivered to the garden centre on Monday and sold by the bag.
Aluminium ribs for the motor housing are ordered from a supplier in Ohio.
The brake disc was invented long ago and is found on nearly every car.
The ceramic pot is glazed in green and signed by the potter on its base.
A thin graphite pencil lay under the desk for a week before anyone noticed.
The greenhouse floor was laid by two brothers who charged very little.
The cloth was woven in a village mill and dyed a deep shade of red.
Crushed stone for the path arrived late, so the workers went home early.

short: feature that aids flow or transfer
notes: Probes: 'improves water drainage' 1.16, 'improve heat dissipation' 1.02, 'better air flow' 0.65; object-only sentences (bought at a market, cost four dollars) 0.00-0.03. But 'are there to improve its appearance' 0.56 (peak ' improve') and 'looks nice and costs little' 0.30: the pole anticipates the function before the flow word arrives.
